meta.note: 🔴 every rhs is DERIVED from this run's base solution — no literal makespan is quoted, because a measured number does not transfer between directories (recompiling re-rolls the assignment DAG).
meta.xa_note: `:xa` is off the LLM emit surface by decision D-9 (C2). The type, the compiler method and referenced_ids remain; the xa_* pair is built by direct type construction. Not a regression.

eq_half_disjunction.note: this is the pair that catches _bigm_half!'s :eq being collapsed back to one unconditional row, which turns ∨ into ∧.
eq_half_disjunction.claim: same argument with the dominated half an :eq — (A ∨ (tF = r_worse)) ≡ A

eq_vs_two_inequalities.note: row COUNTS differ (1 vs 2) on purpose — the gate must not require equal row counts, only non-zero ones. Exercises compile_proposal!'s multi-spec loop.

forbid_window_vs_disjunction.note: near-tautological: _bigm_half!(compiler.jl:158-174) emits rows structurally identical to compile_constraint!(::ForbidWindow)(compiler.jl:38-46) — same orientation, same 1e5 constant. Kept for the record, paired with moved_base, and NOT counted as independent evidence by gate_ng8.py.

scaled_coefficient.note: different matrix row (coefficient 2 vs 1). Diverges if _lin_expr drops or misapplies the coefficient.

dominated_disjunction.note: row structure differs (1 vs 2 + binary); the equality is an argument, not a row identity. Diverges if the Big-M is too small, if the binary polarity is flipped (∨ silently becomes ∧), or if the binary is relaxed to continuous.
dominated_disjunction.claim: B ⟹ A  ⇒  (A ∨ B) ≡ A. native = A alone (1 plain row); grammar = Disjunction(B, A) (2 Big-M rows + 1 binary)

xa_forbid_infeasible.note: 🔴 built by DIRECT TYPE CONSTRUCTION: `:xa` was removed from the emittable surface by C2 (schema · TOOL_SCHEMA · ADVERTISED_VAR_KINDS · prompt · parser) because the prompt ships no candidate-edge list, so the model cannot instantiate a valid (u,v). The type, the compiler method and referenced_ids all REMAIN. That the LLM cannot emit :xa is decision D-9, NOT a regression. 🔴 On this board Xa has ZERO free decision variables (every nonzero is a structural edge pinned to 1 at essential_tg_coponents.jl:1111), so both encodings land on INFEASIBLE. That is agreement on a DISCRIMINATING verdict (base is feasible), but it is NOT evidence that the two forms steer the plan the same way — nothing can steer this axis here.
xa_forbid_infeasible.claim: K rows of `Xa[u,v] = 0` (what compile_constraint!(::ForbidAgent) emits) ≡ one row `Σ Xa[u,v] ≤ 0` (valid because Xa is binary, hence ≥ 0)

compiler_row_count_is_honest.claim: compile_constraint!'s return value equals the rows it actually added

xa_axis_is_degenerate.claim: every Xa nonzero on this board is a structural edge pinned to 1, so `Σ Xa ≥ K` is redundant (base solution survives) while `Σ Xa ≤ 0` is infeasible. Both directions measured.
xa_axis_is_degenerate.expect: n_xa_free == 0 AND the `≥ K` form is feasible AND does not move base

infeasible_row_reaches_solver.claim: tF ≤ -1 must make the MILP INFEASIBLE

noop_row_does_not_move_solution.claim: a row that is already satisfied adds 1 row and changes nothing

dominated_half_is_really_worse.claim: the dominated half B, solved ALONE, must be strictly worse than A alone, and A alone must be strictly worse than base — otherwise the dominated-disjunction pairs prove nothing
dominated_half_is_really_worse.expect: obj(B) > obj(A) + 1 AND obj(B_eq) > obj(A) + 1 AND obj(A) > base + 1

comparison_can_go_red.claim: A vs Disjunction(A_weak, A) — A_weak is satisfied by base, so the disjunction collapses to base and MUST differ from A
comparison_can_go_red.expect: objectives differ by more than RTOL

milp_is_step_invariant.claim: formulate_milp reads `sched`, not `cache` — so stepping the env must not change the MILP. This is why probing at step 0 is not a lucky quote. Measured at 3 checkpoints.
milp_is_step_invariant.expect: same nv / n_constraints / Xa pattern / base objective at every checkpoint
